signals.name: VIX readings contradict each other today — no new figure published, a live lesson in data quality
signals.reading: Multiple queries for today's VIX level returned mutually contradictory numbers (15.41, 15.44, 16.04, 17.62) with no consistent source attribution, and a purported Sep 17 close of ~17.71 directly contradicts this feed's own confirmed Sep 17 intraday read of ~17.05. Rather than publish an unreliable number, this run carries forward the last solidly sourced read (~17.05, Sep 17/26) with the caveat attached
signals.level: No reliable Sep 18/26 VIX print found; last confirmed read ~17.05 (Sep 17/26 intraday)
signals.angle: An honest, transparent data-quality flag is itself a talking point — illustrates why an actively managed, multi-sleeve pool with real due diligence beats mechanically trusting whatever number shows up first in a search

signals.name: Blackstone's BCRED reportedly gates for a third straight quarter
signals.reading: Several independent-looking snippets converge on Q3 repurchase requests of roughly $4.3B (~10% of shares) at Blackstone's $77B BCRED, still capped at 5%, described as a third consecutive quarter of elevated requests (Q1 ~7%, Q2 ~10%, Q3 ~10%) with net outflows near 3% of NAV after $750M in new subscriptions. One key source is dated Sep 3/26 — oddly early for Q3 data given the quarter doesn't end until Sep 30 — so the specific quarter-count framing needs independent verification before it's treated as settled
signals.level: BCRED Q3 requests ~$4.3B (~10% of shares) vs. 5% cap — reported as a third straight quarter, not fully confirmed
signals.angle: If confirmed, three consecutive quarters of gating on the same terms strengthens the 'this is structural, not a one-off' argument for daily liquidity — worth a follow-up check before using the 'third quarter' framing with advisors

signals.name: Barclays' H2 2026 survey reconfirmed: market-neutral and macro remain the two most in-demand strategies
signals.reading: Barclays' survey of 340 investors representing $8.7T in AUM was independently reconfirmed today via a query hitting the actual Barclays page title: 43% expect to be net allocators to hedge funds in H2 2026, Equity Market Neutral remains the most sought-after strategy (29% investor interest), Global Macro second (27%)
signals.level: Market Neutral #1 (29%), Global Macro #2 (27%) investor interest; 43% net allocators, $8.7T surveyed AUM
signals.angle: The most solidly sourced item from today's research — continued third-party validation that CCM8752's two lead sleeves sit in exactly the categories institutional allocators say they want most right now

ELITE.asof: Verified online Sep 18, 2026 via web search (iaclarington.com, newswire.ca, iaconnected.ia.ca and wealthprofessional.ca were all blocked on every attempt today, so everything below is search-snippet level, not a primary-fetch confirmation). The Tej Rai/Alex Bellefleur segregated-funds handover story moved forward, though still short of full confirmation: a new page not seen in prior research — titled 'Segregated funds | Portfolio manager changes now in effect' — surfaced on iaconnected.ia.ca, distinct from the earlier forward-looking 'Change of portfolio managers' notice; the title itself strongly implies the Sep 14/26 handover (4 segregated funds, external managers to Tej Rai/Alex Bellefleur's iAGAM Asset Allocation team, funds renamed, MER expected to decrease, category/risk/objectives unchanged) has now taken effect. However, the page itself remained blocked to direct fetch, so this is the strongest signal yet rather than a settled fact — still worth a direct-browser follow-up when network access allows. No new iA Clarington press release found (most recent remains the Aug 24/26 Active ETF Series distribution announcement, paid Sep 10/26); the Elite Pools & Unified Portfolios Advisor Lunch & Learn events (Sep 22 Ajax/Markham, Sep 23 London, Sep 24 Kitchener, Sep 25 Oakville) remain scheduled, unchanged. On Loomis Sayles: the two Alpha Engine Perspectives pieces flagged yesterday are now identified by title — a Sep 1/26 piece, 'Pursuing Consistent SMID Growth Returns,' on long-term compounding via SMID growth companies, and a Sep 14/26 monthly review covering performance, exposures, and EM credit/FX regime commentary (exact title/URL not resolved) — but full body text of both remains unretrieved via search snippet; a direct WebFetch of loomissayles.com would be needed to extract actual commentary content for an advisor conversation. On PIMCO: no update beyond the Sep 4-5/26 Emmanuel Sharef/PIMCO 60/40 Balanced Income and Growth Fund Asia-rotation story (~$19B AUM, ~60% of equity allocation in Samsung/SK Hynix/TSMC, underweight 'Magnificent Seven'/hyperscalers, beat 97% of peers over 3 years). The macro backdrop feeding all three sub-advisors' positioning sharpened further today: the Bank of Japan hiked 25bp to a 31-year-high 1.25% on a surprising 7-2 split vote (dissenters Asada and Sato, Takaichi-appointed reflationists, wanted a hold), with the yen weakening to ¥156.64 (-0.45%) rather than strengthening — a live, current test of how PIMCO's Asia-heavy positioning and Loomis Sayles's EM/FX regime commentary hold up against an unexpectedly divided G10 central bank. On tariffs: no new development found; the Sep 29/26 outright import ban on Canadian dairy, alcohol and motor vehicles (replacing the 50% Section 338 tariff on those goods, no USMCA exemption) remains on track, confirmed via legal-analysis sources with no news today of a delay or court challenge outcome. iA Clarington overall AUM (>$26B, Jul 31/26) and iAGAM firm-wide AUM ($156B, Jun 30/26) both carried forward unchanged, no fresher figures found today.
ELITE.oneliner: The strongest signal yet that the Tej Rai/Alex Bellefleur segregated-funds handover has completed surfaced today — a new advisor-portal page titled 'now in effect,' though still not independently confirmed via a direct fetch — while the Bank of Japan's own surprising 7-2 split-vote hike to a 31-year-high 1.25% (yen weakening, not strengthening) becomes a live, current test of PIMCO's Asia-heavy positioning inside the Elite Pools, and Loomis Sayles has published its first new commentary since early August.

ELITE.compositionNote: Elite Pools & Unified Portfolios continue to draw on PIMCO, Loomis Sayles and iAGAM as sub-advisors. The structural change at iAGAM — the Asset Allocation team led by Tej Rai and Alex Bellefleur taking over four segregated funds from external managers, effective Sep 14/26 (funds renamed, category/risk/objectives unchanged, MER expected to decrease) — now shows its strongest signal of completion yet: a newly found iaconnected.ia.ca advisor-portal page is titled 'Portfolio manager changes now in effect,' though the page itself remains unconfirmed via direct fetch. On the PIMCO side, the Emmanuel Sharef/PIMCO 60/40 Balanced Income and Growth Fund Asia-rotation story (~$19B AUM, ~60% of equity allocation now Samsung/SK Hynix/TSMC, rotating out of 'Magnificent Seven' US tech) remains the most concrete, current example of sub-advisor positioning, unchanged since Sep 4-5/26 reporting, and is now more topical given today's Bank of Japan surprise. Loomis Sayles has newly published Alpha Engine Perspectives commentary — 'Pursuing Consistent SMID Growth Returns' (Sep 1/26) and an EM credit/FX regime monthly review (Sep 14/26) — its first activity since the Aug 4/26 Municipal Sector Outlook, though full text still needs to be pulled directly. The broader backdrop sharpened again today: the Bank of Japan hiked 25bp to a 31-year-high 1.25% on a surprising 7-2 split vote, weakening the yen rather than strengthening it, a live current test for both PIMCO's Asia-heavy allocation and Loomis Sayles's EM/FX regime views. The Section 338/Canada tariff conflict remains on track for its next escalation — the outright import ban on Canadian dairy/alcohol/motor vehicles still set for Sep 29/26, no new development today. iA Clarington's overall AUM (>$26B, Jul 31/26) and iAGAM's firm-wide AUM ($156B, Jun 30/26) were both carried forward unchanged. iA Clarington has also scheduled four Elite Pools & Unified Portfolios Advisor Lunch & Learn events across Ontario, Sep 22-25/26.
